Compute Match — Signing Up, Signing In and
First-Time Setup
How sign-in works
Compute Match uses Starﬂeet, NVIDIA’s single sign-on service, through Keycloak. Sign up and
Login use the same ﬂow.
1. Open the home page and click Get Started, Sign up or Login.
2. On the /login  page enter your Work email and click Login.
3. Personal email domains (Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail and similar) are blocked with an explanation.
Use your work or enterprise email.
4. You are redirected to Starﬂeet and your organization’s identity provider (for example NVIDIA
corporate login or your company SSO).
5. After authentication you return to Compute Match. You may brieﬂy pass through several
authentication pages; this is normal.
Technically, the frontend uses NextAuth 5 with the Keycloak client customer-web  in the customer
realm, and passes kc_idp_hint=starfleet  to send users to the Starﬂeet identity broker.

First-time checks
After the ﬁrst sign-in you may see one or more of these screens:
Complete Your Proﬁle (customers, /customer/additional-user-details ) or Complete Your
NCP Proﬁle (NCPs, /provider/additional-user-details ). Fill First Name, Last Name,
Organization Name and Phone Number (digits only; +1  is pre-ﬁlled) and click Submit.
Terms and Conditions modal. Scroll to the end, tick the checkbox and click Accept &
Continue, or Sign out. Acceptance is stored as a timestamp on your user ( POST 
/api/v1/users/me/terms-acceptance ).
Thanks for Signing up ( /user-status-pending ). Your account is pending activation; you will
get an email when activated.
Your access is being reviewed ( /access-pending ). Your company is an NVIDIA partner but its
NCP organization is not onboarded yet. A Platform Admin must approve your access request.
Once approved, the page shows Your access has been approved while the session
refreshes.
Access denied ( /access-denied ). Your identity was veriﬁed but you are not authorized. The
page shows your email and the reason. Contact computematchmake@nvidia.com or sign out
and use another work account.
NCP sign-in paths
Welcome email
New NCP users created by NCP onboarding receive a provider_welcome  email with a direct login
link.
Magic link (respond to a reservation)
When a reservation request is routed to an NCP, users in that NCP organization who have the
provider_business_user  role and belong to the offering-validator  group get an email with a magic
link.
1. The link is a Keycloak action token created by the custom accept-reservation-token  extension.
2. Keycloak validates the token and a one-time nonce with the backend ( POST 
/api/v1/offering/validate-nonce ), blocks the link if a different user is already logged in, creates
a session and redirects.
3. The browser lands on /automatic-login?from=magic-link&callbackUrl=... , which skips the email
page and reuses the SSO session, then opens Manage reservation so the NCP can Accept.
4. A magic link is valid for 1 hour. NCPs or admins can resend one ( POST 
/api/v1/provider/offering/{offeringId}/resend-magic-link ) within 7 days of routing.
NPN portal
NVIDIA Partner Network (NPN) members can reach Compute Match directly from the NPN portal
(feature ﬂag NPN_PORTAL_INTEGRATION_ENABLED ). They still pass through the work-email page and
Starﬂeet. If their partner organization is not onboarded yet, an access request with source
NPN_PORTAL  is created and they wait on the access-pending page.
How partner detection works
Compute Match keeps a partner domain mirror of email domains belonging to NVIDIA
partners, synced from Salesforce twice a day.
Domain lookup statuses are PARTNER , NOT_PARTNER  and PENDING .
Personal mail providers can never be partner domains.
When a user from a partner domain signs up and their NCP is not onboarded, POST 
/api/v1/user  creates an access request (statuses PENDING , APPROVED , REJECTED ; sources
NPN_PORTAL , SIGNUP ).
A Platform Admin approves or rejects it under Onboard NCPs →  Review Onboarding
Requests. Approval provisions the organization and user in Keycloak; rejection emails the
reason. A rejected applicant can apply again, which creates a new request.
Signing out
Use Logout in the account menu. If your session cannot be refreshed, the app shows a recovery
screen and performs a full Keycloak logout.
